title: Container With Most Water
statement: Given heights of vertical lines at indices 0..n-1, return the maximum water area formed by two lines: area = min(height[i], height[j]) * (j - i).

predict_steps.prompt: If height[left] < height[right], which pointer should move?
predict_steps.hint: The shorter side limits the area.

viva.question: Why is the two-pointer area search linear instead of checking every pair?
expected_points: pointers start at both ends and only move inward
each index is discarded at most once
total steps stay linear in the number of lines
a nested pair loop would be quadratic

viva.question: What is the area when every height is zero?
expected_points: the min height is always zero
every candidate area collapses to zero
width alone cannot store water without height

viva.question: Why move the pointer at the shorter line rather than the taller one?
expected_points: width shrinks either way so you need a taller min height to improve
the short side is the bottleneck for the current pair
moving the taller side cannot raise the min height by itself
discarding the short side is the only move that might raise the limiting height
